text:
Oncall Bot: :rotating_light: alert: 5 nodes in us-west-2 reporting block device errors after firmware update. GPU provisioning failures detected.

Chris (infra): seeing kernel oops and nvme resets on those hosts, jobs failing with i/o error. reassigning affected nodes to maintenance pool.

Maya: ugh — which fleet? can you paste dmesg tail?

Chris (infra): pasting a few lines — looks like repeated I/O timeout + sg errors:
```
[ 1234.567890] nvme nvme0: I/O 0 QID 1 timeout, aborting
[ 1234.568001] nvme nvme0: abort status: 0x2
[ 1234.568200] blk_update_request: I/O error, dev nvme0n1, sector 12345678
[ 1234.568900] sd 8:0:0:0: [nvme0n1] READ_UNCORRECTABLE error
```

Linh: same pattern on two other hosts. These devices were in the host-fleet that got FW 2.4.1 last night.

Dave: are we sure it's the firmware and not a bulk scrub/job pattern getting heavy random small reads? Any sudden IOPS spike?

Chris (infra): Cloud metrics show an IOPS jump on those nodes ~30s before the errors, but nothing that should cause device panic — looks like devices start flapping after a couple hundred thousand small reads.

Maya: immediate mitigation: cordon + drain the affected nodes, add them to a temporary blackhole pool so provisioner won't schedule GPUs there. I can run cordon now.

Chris (infra): done — cordoned and blackholed, jobs draining. Also pushed a policy to route new GPU requests to us-west-1 and eu-west-1 for now. Not ideal but keeps user jobs running.

Linh: cheaper fix? rollback firmware to 2.4.0 for these SKUs? That would require maintenance window and node reboots.

Dave: rollback is safest long-term. Short-term: can we set local-ssd scrub offload to reduce random read amplification? Maybe change batch size and caching so we don't hammer metadata. But that's risky.

Maya: also noticed scheduler retried pods to eu-west-1 causing cross-region egress for mixed workloads — customers with pinned data saw failures. We need a routing exception for data-local jobs.

Chris (infra): opened infra ticket INF-4321 to track rollback + root cause. Plan: 1) keep nodes blackholed, 2) schedule rolling reboots with FW rollback next maintenance window (02:00 UTC), 3) run targeted block-level scrub and SMART extended tests, 4) postmortem and quantize devices that fail.

Linh: adding a quick health-check job to detect early flapping and auto-take device offline before kernel panics. I can prototype a lightprobe that does an nvme identify + short read.

Dave: FYI cost note — routing to other regions pushed up spot usage and we hit a transient $8k/day uplift for GPU jobs. We'll flag finance and consider temporary credit for impacted customers.

Maya: assigning ops rotation to monitor overnight. tagging @oncall to follow-up with rollback approval.

Oncall Bot: assigned to Maya and Chris for the 03:00 UTC window.

Chris (infra): quick checklist posted to INF-4321. will update thread with results of the first rollback batch. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
